automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public sources published or visibly updated within the last 2 days relative to run_timestamp; exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice, workflow, governance, verification, adoption, and implementation lenses only.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub added total pull-request merge counts by AI adoption phase to enterprise and organization Copilot usage reports, complementing existing per-user averages.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Team adoption measurement can move beyond usage counts into outcome instrumentation by cohort, which supports operating-model reviews and evaluation of whether AI-assisted development changes merge throughput.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Record only the adoption-metrics practice implication locally; broad Copilot product coverage belongs upstream.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub made MAI-Code-1-Flash generally available for Copilot Business and Enterprise, with administrator enablement through Copilot policy settings and usage-based billing.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Coding-agent model selection is becoming an administrative control surface; local practice should treat low-latency model enablement as a governed policy and cost decision rather than an individual developer preference.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product and model details upstream; local implication is model-policy governance for iterative agentic coding workflows.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub Desktop 3.6 added worktree support and expanded Copilot-backed commit authoring and merge-conflict assistance, including model selection and bring-your-own-key support.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Worktrees and assisted conflict resolution are becoming standard UI-level source-workflow primitives for parallel agent and human work; local guidance should emphasize clean workspace isolation and repository-standard commit authorship.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product release details upstream; local implication is source-workflow design for multi-branch and agent-assisted development.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Copilot code review added organization-level default review depth and now uses built-in CLI and SDK file-exploration tools such as grep, rg, glob, and view in its review path.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: AI review quality depends on explicit retrieval depth, source-exploration tools, and visibility into review effort; local review rubrics should capture review-depth defaults and repository overrides.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product mechanics upstream; local implication is review-depth governance and retrieval-tool evidence practice.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Enterprise-managed settings for GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code added a strictKnownMarketplaces control that limits plugin installation to explicitly defined marketplaces.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Plugin and tool extension governance is shifting earlier in the agent lifecycle, before tool execution; local governance should cover approved marketplaces, install consent, and untrusted-plugin risk.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep tool/product coverage upstream; local implication is governed plugin marketplace policy for coding-agent clients.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub Actions administrators can disable standard hosted-runner labels and add macOS runners to runner groups.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Evaluation and repair harnesses that run AI-generated code need stricter control over which compute environments agents and tests can consume; runner groups can encode policy boundaries for privileged or costly environments.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep CI platform release details upstream; local implication is harness and permission architecture for agent-run verification.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: GitHub Actions added workflow syntax for running steps concurrently while retaining separate logs and execution.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agent repair loops and evaluation harnesses often need concurrent services, test watchers, or instrumentation; native parallel steps reduce ad hoc shell backgrounding and make logs easier to audit.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep platform syntax details upstream; local implication is harness design with auditable concurrent setup.

visible_dates.basis: GitHub Changelog page date and changelog feed pubDate

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: npm added a temporary read-only safeguard for high-impact accounts after sensitive account changes such as email changes or 2FA recovery-code use.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Agentic coding workflows that install, update, or publish packages should treat package-install and publishing paths as supply-chain risk surfaces, with approval gates for dependency changes and registry-affecting actions.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep registry and product details upstream; local implication is supply-chain governance for agent package operations.

visible_dates.basis: npm registry public time field for version 2.1.195

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Claude Code 2.1.195 fixed project-settings plugin enablement paths that did not require explicit install consent, fixed background agent visibility and restart issues, and improved remote session startup with a provisioning checklist.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Durable agent instructions and project settings can implicitly activate plugins, so local practice should require explicit install consent and expose remote-startup progress when agent environments are provisioned.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep release and product details upstream; local implication is consent and progress instrumentation around project-level agent extensions.

visible_dates.basis: npm registry public time field for version 2.1.193

qualifying_findings.short_factual_summary: Claude Code 2.1.193 added all-shell auto-mode classification, denial reasons in transcripts and permissions UI, assistant-response telemetry controls, MCP authentication notices, and background shell memory-pressure reaping.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Permission systems are becoming auditable artifacts: denial reasons, transcript entries, telemetry redaction, MCP authentication notices, and background-process cleanup all affect governance of tool calls and long-running agents.
qualifying_findings.routing_note: Keep product and protocol coverage upstream; local implication is auditability of tool-call permissions, telemetry, and long-running shell management.
